gap: No result ChatGPT got states that QIDI's current Plus4 firmware limits the 400 W chamber heater to 40% duty (max_power 0.4, roughly 160 W) and holds chamber heating until the bed reaches temperature, while the QIDI Q2 firmware lets its 280 W chamber heater run at full power (max_power 1). That makes the '~5–8 min' Plus4 chamber figure ChatGPT used a poor guide to a Plus4 running current firmware.
standout_why: Compared against us.qidi3d.com Plus4 TechSpecs (cited), desktop3dprinters.us chamber-temperature list (cited) and 3dcalculators.com enclosure-heating post (cited). The QIDI spec page lists only '450W+400W(Chamber Heating)'. The desktop3dprinters page has no heater power, warm-up time or firmware detail. 3dcalculators has an owner test showing a 25-minute warm-up at 40% heater power and 16.5 minutes at 70%, but it does not say that 40% is QIDI's shipped firmware setting or that chamber heating waits for the bed. None of them compares firmware limits across QIDI models. yakja.co could not be read (TLS certificate error), so it was not checked.
decides: It weakens ChatGPT's pick of the Plus4 for 'fastest chamber heating'. On current firmware the Plus4's usable chamber heater power (0.4 × 400 W ≈ 160 W) is below the Q2's uncapped 280 W, and the Plus4 heats bed and chamber one after the other rather than together. Any warm-up time for the Plus4 should name the firmware and power setting. The fast 5–8 min figures come from before the cap or from unstated conditions. This finding does not by itself prove the Q2 heats its chamber faster, because the Q2 has a smaller chamber and nobody has published a timed Q2 test.

findings.label: Chamber heater firmware power cap
findings.value: max_power 0.4 (40% duty); with the 400 W rated heater that is about 160 W average maximum
findings.note: From the [heater_generic chamber] section: 'max_power:0.4', 'heat_with_heater_bed:True', 'heat_with_heater_bed_tem_add:25', target_min_temp 45, target_max_temp 65. [heater_bed] max_power is 1.0. 160 W = 0.4 × 400 W, taking the 400 W from QIDI's spec page and assuming average power scales linearly with PWM duty. The file has no separate 110 V and 220 V entries.

findings.label: Chamber heating sequencing (firmware)
findings.value: Chamber heating starts only once the heated bed reaches its set temperature (firmware V1.6.0 and later)
findings.note: Plus4_V1.6.0 release note: 'Optimized chamber heating logic: chamber heating starts only when the heated bed reaches the specified temperature.' Total warm-up is therefore bed time plus chamber time, not the two at once. The repo README lists V1.7.1 as the latest.

findings.note: Maker spec page. Chamber up to 65 °C (PTC heater, 2nd gen). Gives no heat-up times.

findings.label: 110 V region hardware issue
findings.value: QIDI offered replacement heater power boards and extended warranties to Plus4 owners in 110 V countries
findings.source_title: Plus4 Issue Prompts Qidi Tech to Offer Replacement Parts (All3DP, Matthew Mensley, 2024-11-07)
findings.note: All3DP: 'An issue affecting the new Plus4 3D printer in 110V countries accelerates wear on a power-carrying component.' This US-region issue is the reported background to the firmware power cap; QIDI's own announcement was not found.

findings.label: Chamber heater firmware power cap
findings.value: max_power 1 (full power; 280 W rated chamber heater), no heat_with_heater_bed line
findings.note: [heater_generic chamber]: heater_pin PC8, max_power:1, max_temp 70. [heater_bed] max_power 1.0. Unlike the Plus4 file, there is no bed-first chamber setting.

findings.value: 150 W + 550 W (chamber heating) + 500 W (heatbed); 110 V / 220–240 V AC, region-specific models; runs at full power about 3–5 min during warm-up
findings.source_title: QIDI Plus5 TechSpecs – QIDI US Store

The page tells buyers to check the label by the power socket to confirm the supply matches the printer's rating. The 3–5 min full-power phase is described for bed warm-up; no chamber time is given.
